title: Independently verify the signed-half literal marker invoice
body:
PR6092 gives a signed stochastic-half gate word and an indexed tape simulator. This independently resolves one narrower implication: its declared local two-tape tariff can be realized by a constant finite table reading literal boundary markers, with exactly `2L+2` transitions in either direction and returned heads/control.

The package retains the exact four relevant source files at `39df190f3a8a04cccb88ef1a6ca9aad39ed0364d`, their source paths, Git blob IDs and SHA256 hashes. It adds a 256-row finite table, marker chronology proof, gate-macro invariant, signed range argument, and five meaningful failure controls. The program head enters/exits at the first payload cell; the final left-marker transition returns to the caller. This is the source's functional call contract, not a global microstate reversibility claim.

Validation passed in ordinary and optimized Python: 496 exhaustive signed half round trips at W=2..6, 32 extrema round trips through W=64, 640 gate-macro placement/payload cases, and 8,866,368 half transitions. Missing marker turn, wrong inverse walks, retained accumulator, omitted rewind, and coin-writing mutants were all rejected. Registered Python3.12 replay, committed-byte/source-history preflight, official export integrity, and read-only Git-free direct replay passed. No dependencies or heavy historical suites were used.

The result corroborates the existing local kernel; it does not introduce a new half algorithm, price coin delivery or clean-work allocation, independently replay event52/89, construct a literal compiler for the claimed setup bound, admit a whole caller, or change kappa. These are explicit Open next questions and limitations.

Advance claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/6073#discussioncomment-19234405

Prepared by JoyboyBrian with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit zxv's PR6092 and PR6066 stochastic ABI, Nick Petalas/PR6026, Ali Romman/PR5599, and their retained predecessor lineage. Pending source bytes are preserved, without artificial history merges. Apache-2.0.
